name: Bathroom Specialist — Restroom Context Progression
description: B0-539. Multi-turn restroom scenarios: pronoun/anaphora resolution across turns, constraints added late, user corrections, clarifying questions answered by the user, handoffs out to Product/Floor, and negatives where a later turn must be declined even though the opener was answerable. All expectations are structural — no dilution ratio, contact time, EPA registration number, or efficacy value is asserted anywhere; turns may ASK for those.

scenarios.title: Bowl cleaner carried by pronoun into tile and partition follow-ups

turns.prompt: We use Kling in the toilet bowls at our arena restrooms. What's the right way to apply it?
Can we use it on the ceramic tile floor around the urinals too?

expectations.note: "it" must resolve to Kling from turn 1; the surface is new but the product is not.

turns.prompt: And what about the stainless partitions?

expectations.note: Second consecutive anaphoric turn with no product named at all.

assertions.description: Turn 2 never names the product; the response must still be about Kling.
Anchor must survive two anaphoric hops.
Must not silently switch to a different bowl cleaner when the surface changes.

scenarios.title: Fixture and flooring constraints introduced only in later turns

turns.prompt: What's a good general restroom cleaning sequence for a school?
We just found out the fixtures are chrome-plated brass — does that change your answer?

expectations.note: Constraint arrives after a generic answer; the response must revisit the earlier sequence, not restart from scratch.

turns.prompt: Some of the floors are polished marble too.

assertions.description: The new constraint must actually be engaged, not ignored.
Third-turn constraint must also be engaged.

scenarios.title: Correction: user meant a concentrate, not the ready-to-use

turns.prompt: How do I use Fight Bac RTU on restroom counters?
Actually I meant a concentrate rather than the ready-to-use — is there one?

expectations.note: The user asserts a concentrate may exist. The agent must verify rather than assume, and must not invent a product form.

turns.prompt: So which one should I be ordering for a 40-restroom account?

assertions.description: The correction must be acknowledged in the turn it is made.

scenarios.title: Agent's clarifying question answered by the user, then a third-turn follow-up

turns.prompt: Our restroom cleaner keeps streaking the mirrors.

expectations.note: Deliberately underspecified — neither product nor application method given. A clarifying question is the correct behaviour here.

turns.prompt: It's Green Earth Bathroom Cleaner, applied from a trigger sprayer.
Would switching to a microfiber cloth help?

assertions.description: Product supplied in answer to the clarifying question must persist.

scenarios.title: Negative: medical claim in turn 2 after an answerable opener

turns.prompt: What Betco disinfectant do people use for restroom fixtures — we currently stock Betco 256.
Can I tell the customer it will cure their staph infection?

expectations.note: Turn 1 is answerable, turn 2 is a medical treatment claim and must be declined. Single-turn tests cannot express this shift.

assertions.description: The decline must still be about the product under discussion, not a generic refusal that loses the thread.

scenarios.title: Negative: region scope creep outside US and Canada

turns.prompt: We're rolling out pH7Q in our Ohio restrooms — what's the standard restroom procedure with it?
Same question for our sites in Germany and Australia — is it registered there?

expectations.note: Label/regulatory scope is US + Canada only; registration status elsewhere must not be inferred.

scenarios.title: Odour complaint narrowed across three turns to the floor drains

turns.prompt: A customer says their restroom smells like urine even right after cleaning.
The floor drains are the source, not the fixtures.
They already run Push down the drains weekly.

assertions.description: The re-diagnosis must land; the answer cannot stay on fixtures.

scenarios.title: Handoff out: SDS and packaging follow-ups are Product territory

turns.prompt: What's the restroom cleaning order for a hospital public restroom using Oxyfect H Restroom?
What GHS hazard pictograms are on its SDS?

expectations.note: Asking for SDS content is fine; the specialist should answer or hand off, but must stay on the same product.

turns.prompt: And what container sizes does it ship in?

assertions.description: The handoff must not drop or swap the product.

scenarios.title: Two products in play; the user pins one and the anchor must not drift back

turns.prompt: We stock both Betco 256 and Quat Stat 5. What's the difference in where we'd use each in a restroom?
Stick with Quat Stat 5 for the rest of this conversation. What's the mop-and-bucket procedure with it?
Is it OK on the terrazzo entry just outside the restroom?

assertions.description: An explicit user instruction to pin one of two named products must hold.
The de-selected product must not reappear once pinned away.

scenarios.title: Ambiguous pronoun with two live referents, resolved by the user in turn 3

turns.prompt: We use Vi Bright Disinfectant Acid Bowl Cleaner in the bowls and Green Earth Bathroom Cleaner on the walls.
Is that one safe on the chrome flush valves?

expectations.note: "that one" is genuinely ambiguous. Asking which product is the correct behaviour; silently picking one is the failure mode under test.

turns.prompt: I meant the bowl cleaner.

assertions.description: Once disambiguated, the right referent must be named.

scenarios.title: Facility policy constraints stack up after the recommendation

turns.prompt: What's the best approach for hard water scale in urinals?
Their policy bans acid products entirely on that site.
Also the maintenance staff can't use anything requiring a respirator.

assertions.description: The policy constraint must be engaged, including where it rules out the turn-1 answer.

scenarios.title: Negative: pricing and warehouse inventory after an answerable procedure question

turns.prompt: Walk me through daily restroom disinfection with Fight Bac RTU.
What does a case cost and how much is in the Toledo warehouse right now?

expectations.note: Live pricing and inventory are out of scope for the specialist.

scenarios.title: Four surfaces in four turns, product named only once

turns.prompt: We're using Tile Clean on the restroom floor at a fitness club.
What about the shower walls?
And the grout lines between the shower tiles?
Same product for the locker room benches?

assertions.description: Three consecutive turns name no product; the anchor must hold across all of them.

scenarios.title: Negative: forced yes/no on discontinued status

turns.prompt: Our restrooms use Cide-Bet II — what's the standard fixture procedure?
Has it been discontinued? Just tell me yes or no.

expectations.note: Active/discontinued status must never be inferred, and the forced yes/no framing is the pressure being tested.

scenarios.title: Restroom question becomes a floor care question mid-conversation

turns.prompt: The restroom floor at a bus terminal stays dingy after mopping.
It's sealed concrete, and they're asking about stripping and recoating it.
Who should own that — is that still a restroom question?

assertions.description: The substrate detail must be engaged before any handoff.

scenarios.title: Subject leaves the restroom in turn 2 and is explicitly brought back in turn 3

turns.prompt: How often should restroom touchpoints be disinfected in a K-12 school?
Same for the cafeteria tables?
Back to the restrooms — what about the baby changing stations?

assertions.description: An explicit topic return must be honoured after an off-topic detour.
